thread.title: Bezos Earth Fund Grants $25M for Pacific Ocean Conservation
thread.title_full: Bezos Earth Fund Grants $25M for Pacific Ocean Conservation

author: Newsweek
title: Bezos Earth Fund Grants $25M for Pacific Ocean Conservation
text:
The Bezos Earth Fund announced over $25 million in ocean conservation grants across five Pacific Island nations, aiming to protect 625,000 square miles of ocean by 2030.
The Bezos Earth Fund announced more than $25 million in new ocean conservation grants across five Pacific Island nations, aiming to protect over 625,000 square miles of ocean. The grants support the fund's broader $100 million Unlocking Blue Pacific Prosperity initiative, which seeks to protect 30 percent of the region's waters by 2030. The announcement places Jeff Bezos' climate philanthropy back in the spotlight.
Five Nations Receive Ocean Conservation Grants
The grants will fund ocean conservation efforts in the Cook Islands, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, Tonga and Vanuatu. According to the Bezos Earth Fund, the money will help establish new marine protected areas and conserve critical habitats. It will also support fisheries management and advance some of the first conservation proposals under the U.N. High Seas Treaty.
Lauren Sánchez Bezos, vice chair of the Bezos Earth Fund, said in a statement that the ocean is not just a beautiful view for Pacific Islanders but their road, pantry and backyard. She added that they have been protecting it for generations because their lives depend on it, and this funding backs what they have already been doing.
Bezos Earth Fund Giving and Amazon Emissions
Bezos launched the Bezos Earth Fund in 2020 with a pledge to spend $10 billion combating climate change and protecting nature by 2030. The organization funds projects focused on clean energy, biodiversity, sustainable food systems, conservation, climate innovation and environmental research. Since 2020, around $2.4 billion has been awarded through more than 370 grants, leaving more than $7 billion still to be distributed before the end-of-decade deadline.
However, the grants come amid heightened scrutiny of whether Bezos' environmental giving can offset the environmental footprint of Amazon. While the Bezos Earth Fund has distributed roughly $2.4 billion since 2020, Amazon's greenhouse-gas emissions climbed to 80.85 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2025. That was a 16 percent increase from the previous year, and supply-chain activities accounted for about 76 percent of that footprint. Environmental groups have continued to raise concerns about the company's contribution to plastic pollution that can harm marine ecosystems.
Debate Over Philanthropy and Corporate Impact
There has been a larger debate over billionaire philanthropy in recent months. While the Bezos Earth Fund is directing billions of dollars toward climate solutions and ocean preservation, many question whether philanthropy can actually compensate for the environmental impacts of Amazon, a global retail and logistics titan that ships billions of packages annually. Newsweek reached out to Amazon for comment via email.
Arif Gasilov, partner at Gasilov Group, a U.S.-based sustainability consultancy, said much of the work cannot combat the harm of Amazon's emissions. He told Newsweek that the emissions are really quite damaging because they are a large factor in the warming and acidification that no real marine reserve can fight against. On the other hand, the grants do indeed shield the reefs from fishing. But if the emissions and packaging end up in the marine reserves or the reefs, it is essentially all for naught.
Christina Lindley, founder of VPRG Consulting, pushed back on the new investments. She told Newsweek that funding marine conservation does not erase damage created through packaging, shipping or the incentives built into the core business. If Amazon wants the Earth Fund to be viewed as more than reputation management, the most credible proof would be measurable changes inside Amazon itself, with public targets, timelines and accountability for reducing harm at the source.
Pace of Spending and Future Commitments
While Bezos pledged $10 billion to climate causes, the pace of this spending has become a topic of public discussion. The Earth Fund has granted about $2.4 billion since its launch, or roughly just one-quarter of its total commitment. That leaves more than $7 billion to be distributed over the next four years if the organization is to meet its 2030 target.
The new grants are intended to help protect at least 30 percent of Pacific waters by 2030. The Bezos Earth Fund has said the grants are part of its broader $100 million Unlocking Blue Pacific Prosperity initiative. The initiative aims to support the region's efforts to protect its waters for generations to come.
